selected_leaf: Test whether ordering alone can guarantee exactly-once publication when a valid unconsumed witness authorizes a non-idempotent publication and the durable consumed-witness marker is stored separately, with a crash allowed between the two durable effects.

bounded_leaf_result.tested_scope: Deterministic two-effect state machine with one valid unconsumed witness W, one non-idempotent externally visible publication P, one separately durable consumed marker M, and fail-stop crash/restart allowed after either durable effect. Retry reconstructs state only from durable role-local marker state and the unchanged witness.

ordering_tests.retry_observation: Witness still appears unconsumed, so an identical retry remains eligible under marker-only reconstruction.
Witness appears consumed, so retry suppresses publication.

A durable prepare intent proves an attempt was authorized but does not distinguish whether non-idempotent P durably happened unless P itself exposes an idempotent lookup/key or shares the transaction.

bounded_leaf_result.direct_architecture_conclusion: No ordering of two separately durable effects can guarantee both no duplicate and no loss across the crash window. Exactly-once requires an additional primitive that collapses the ambiguity: either target-side idempotency keyed by the witness/attempt identity, a readable publication receipt that uniquely proves the effect, or atomic fusion of publication and consumed-marker state in one transactional/CAS commit.
bounded_leaf_result.unresolved_capability: A zero-cost, zero-finite-quota Chat-capable atomicity primitive binding externally visible publication to witness consumption, or equivalent target-side idempotency/readback semantics. Without one, generic external non-idempotent publication remains unresolved.
bounded_leaf_result.semantic_claim: Within the exact deterministic fixture, ordering alone cannot remove the crash window: publication-first admits duplication; marker-first admits loss; adding a prepare record does not disambiguate whether publication committed.
not_proven: impossibility for targets that natively support idempotency keys
impossibility when publication and marker can be fused into one repository transaction
arbitrary distributed protocols with stronger target readback semantics
